contexts.text: If truths and goods are not present... the man yields (or succumbs).
In temptations, the Angels defend the man's falsities and evils, otherwise he would yield. Explained.
They who, in temptations, do not resist in freedom, yield.

(Yielding in temptations. See Temptation.) AC 2689:3. AC 3488:7. AC 3652:6. AC 3927:3. AC 4274:2. AC 5044:2. AC 5246:4. AC 5280:4. AC 7854:end. AC 8159:end. AC 8165:end. AC 8169. AC 8172. AC 8179:3. AC 8358. AC 8588. TCR 597:2.
How, of itself (the Church militant) yields, but conquers from the Lord. Treated of. AC 2714:4.
(Such) would yield at once; and they who yield come into the confirmation of evil and the persuasion of falsity. Explained. AC 5280:4.
If (in combats) the man breaks (the bonds of conscience), he yields; and, if he yields in this way, it is all over with his salvation.
Those who have yielded in temptations. Signified.
They who yield in temptations come into a state of condemnation. Explained.
He who believes... that he can resist from his own forces, yields.
That they yield when they look downwards (represented by) the sons of Israel yielding when Moses let down his hands.
These Genii... only attack... when it appears that the man is falling so as to yield: they are then suddenly present, and impel him to fall altogether. AC 8594:end.
The reason the faith that looks... to self and the world, yields, is that the man then fights from himself.

(Such a one) is not admitted into any combat, because he yields; and if a man yields, his state after temptation is worse than that before it; because evil has then acquired power over good, and falsity over truth. AC 8975.
That they who place merit in works, yield in temptations. References.
That these will not afterwards yield to evils and falsities from Hell. Signified. (by not being hurt by the second death.) AE 128.
That those who... do not yield when tempted by the Babylonians and dragonists, will come into Heaven... Signified, Explained.
At this day... Hell assaults all such with diabolical fury, so that unless the Lord resisted... the man could not but yield.
Since the Council of Nice, if anyone had been admitted (into spiritual temptation) he would have at once yielded, and would thus have precipitated himself more deeply into Hell.
That (the dragonists) yielded. Signified, Explained.
